- $\sigma_t(t)$: The function returning the actual extinction coefficient at distance $t$ [S1].

The claim states that $σ_t(t)$ is the function returning the actual extinction coefficient at distance $t$. In the provided source [S1], the pseudocode for `drt_sample` includes the line `Tr *= 1 - (sr_t(t_run) / sr)`. The variable `Tr` represents the transmittance estimate, which is updated by multiplying by the probability of not interacting with a particle. The term `(sr_t(t_run) / sr)` represents the ratio of the actual extinction coefficient to the majorant (homogenized medium density). Therefore, `sr_t(t_run)` corresponds to the actual extinction coefficient at the current position `t_run`. The notes also explicitly mention `σ_t(t_{run})` in the context of updating transmittance, confirming that $σ_t$ represents the actual extinction coefficient.
